title: Explainable Fuzzy Neural Network with Multi-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning for Micro-Architecture Design Space Exploration
problem: Modern micro-architecture designs have vast design spaces that are difficult to explore manually. Existing DSE algorithms like Bayesian Optimization and ensemble learning suffer from poor interpretability, preventing designers from understanding the decision-making process.
motivation: Interpretability and efficiency in design space exploration are critical for validating and understanding micro-architecture design decisions.
method: The approach uses Fuzzy Neural Networks to extract simple, human-readable rules that explain what the system learned about good micro-architecture designs. It combines this with multi-fidelity reinforcement learning, which uses cheap, quick but less-precise simulations to explore broadly, and saves expensive, accurate simulations for verifying the most promising options. Together, this makes the design process both faster (requiring fewer expensive simulations) and more transparent (designers understand why certain designs are recommended).
key_novelty: The core idea is combining Fuzzy Neural Networks with multi-fidelity reinforcement learning so designers can understand why certain micro-architecture designs are recommended while exploring the design space with fewer expensive simulations.
contributions: Fuzzy Neural Networks for inducing interpretable knowledge from DSE processes
Multi-fidelity reinforcement learning approach that reduces reliance on costly simulations
Achieves state-of-the-art results with limited sample budgets

metrics.other: DSE sample efficiency, design quality surpasses state-of-the-art

primary_theme: interpretable and efficient design space exploration
